findings.reason: the section must correct the mischaracterised grammar and either pin the document check's before/after output on dotted, hyphenated and bare ids or state why its grammar is exempt from the single core, because otherwise the consolidation silently changes which headings `_implementable_section_ids` counts as sections.
findings.text: §17 states that `doccheck._NUMBERED_SECTION_ID` "full-matches heading ids" and "accept[s] only the dotted or bare numbered form"; the regex at `reckon/doccheck.py:135` is `re.compile(r"s[1-9][0-9]*")`, which accepts neither a dotted nor a bare form — it requires the `s` prefix and forbids every separator, so `s5.1`, `s5-1` and `5` all fail its `fullmatch` today. Folding it onto routing's `_SECTION_IDENTITY` core (`reckon/crew/routing.py:219`, `^(?:§|#)?\s*(?:s(?:ection)?[\s.-]*)?(\d+(?:[.-]\d+)*)$`) is therefore not the neutral "same grammar answers" the section claims: it widens the document check's recognised section set to bare `5`, `§5`, `section 5`, `s5.1` and `s5-1`, and §17 pins the before/after outputs only for the ledger and the evidence key, not for the document check, even though two plans in this project already carry dotted section ids.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 keeps one private span parser behind one public reader (`plan_headings`) with `structured_section_spans` as a projection of it, and §16 hides the section set, the digest map and the coverage join behind `_section_digests` and one module-private predicate.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §16/§17/§18 consolidate owners rather than fork them (section identity to `reckon/_plan_html.py`, the landing rule to `reckon/_schema.py`, the `c-run-` prefix to `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`), and each names the file it extends; the two identity-adjacent helpers (`evidence._section_key`, `ledger.normalize_section`) are kept with a stated distinct output.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16, §17 and §18 each carry an interface-accounting paragraph that names its additions (three public definitions across the three: the heading reader and machinery predicate in §17, the classification predicate in §18) and states why nothing can be retired.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the section-grammar and heading-walk machinery it names, but mischaracterises one existing regex it is about to fold onto a shared core, so the one-grammar rule rests on a false premise.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the coverage predicate is justified as a join over two existing readers that "adds no walk of its own", `structured_section_spans` is retained because it has callers outside the module, and no proposed layer merely forwards to existing machinery.
